cases.brief:
Connector catalog: one registry, a two-pane Add connection dialog, and a status for each connection (CTX-1078) (#565)

* Connectors list: give the status of each connection (CTX-1078)

GET /:orgSlug/api/v1/connectors now gives a status for each item:
connected, needs_reconnect, or setup_pending. The rule reads the stored
connection row only, with the same rule as the isInstalled field of each
provider status route. Thus the connector catalog can show one state for
each provider without a status read for each connection.

An integration test on a real database seeds a row for each state of
each provider and checks the status in the list.


* Connectors list: keep the status type in its module (CTX-1078)

No other module reads the type, so knip reports the export.


* Connector cards: give each card a stable connection hook (CTX-1078)

ConnectorListItem sets data-connection-id on each card, and shows a
short teal mark while data-marked is set. The catalog Fix action finds
the card with this hook, not with a text search.


* Connectors: add the connector catalog (CTX-1078)

Add connection is now a two-pane dialog that reads one registry
(features/connectors/catalog/registry.tsx). The left pane has the views
All, Connected, one view for each group, and Coming soon, each with a
count. The right pane has one row for each connector, with the worst
state of its connections and one action: Connect, Add another, or Ask
for it. A row with a connection that needs a reconnect or has an
unfinished setup also has Fix. Fix closes the catalog, scrolls to the
card of that connection, and marks it for a moment. A search in the
header shows matches from all groups.

The Connectors page gives one setup opener for each connector type, in
place of the list of Add buttons. Each setup dialog and its open state
stay as they were. The Add buttons and the old catalog dialog are
removed. Ask for it records a connector_request action through the
HyperDX browser client, which adds the org and the user, and shows a
toast.

Stories with plays cover a new org, a busy org, the Coming soon view,
a search with no match, Ask for it, and Fix on the Connectors page.


* Docs: describe the connector catalog (CTX-1078)

The connections guide tells the user to choose Connect on the row of the
tool, and to search or select a group. The Confluence guide uses the
product name only. Add a changeset for the release.


* Connectors list: test more stored states (CTX-1078)

Add seeds for rows from before the status key (Linear and PagerDuty),
installed rows without the site or the token (Confluence, Slack, Linear,
Notion), a hosted GitHub draft without App credentials, and empty Linear
and PagerDuty drafts that the list must not show.


* Connectors: one install rule for each provider (CTX-1078)

The connectors list copied the isInstalled rule of each status route by
hand on raw JSON. Now models/connection-status.ts has one install rule
for each provider. The list applies the rule to the parsed stored config.
The Confluence, Slack, Notion, and PagerDuty status routes apply the same
rule to the connection that they resolve. Linear keeps
linearConnectionIsInstalled for both. The status values are one const
array: the TypeScript type and the z.enum of the route come from it.

(ariaHideOutside). It keeps only the live announcer and the elements
with data-react-aria-top-layer. The root Toaster is now in such an
element, so that a screen reader announces the "Ask for it" toast of
the connector catalog, and each other toast that shows over a modal.

Each available entry has an async start: it makes any draft, then gives
the setup that the page opens, or nothing when the start runs on its own
(the GitHub App popup). useConnectorStart has no GitHub branch, and the
Connectors page has no opener for each connector: it keeps one setup
state for its mounted setup dialogs. The display order of the cards
comes from the registry order.

The catalog rows switch on the availability with a never check, so a new
availability makes TypeScript show each place to handle. A row shows
its state with ConnectorHealthIndicator, the same chip as the cards; only
the "N connected" label is new.

Fix sets a marked connection in the page state. The card shows a ring
and the hidden text "Needs your attention" on its expand control, and
after the modal closes it scrolls into view and takes the focus. The mark
goes after 2 s. Each card has one connection anchor id
(connectionAnchorId), which Fix and the new GitHub draft scroll use.

Also: remove the onFlowStarted and onDraftCreated options of
useGithubConnectFlow and onInstallFlowStarted of the self-hosted wizard,
which no caller used. Tests and plays take the view counts from the
registry. The GitHub card story gets its args, so its 4 allowed type
errors go.


* Confluence card: show the product name only (CTX-1078)

The card said "Atlassian Confluence" and the catalog says "Confluence".
The card now says "Confluence" too. The plays read the new name.


* Docs: start each connector from its catalog row (CTX-1078)

Each page that said "Add connection, then <Provider>" or "Connectors ->
Add connection -> <Provider>" now says: select Add connection, then
select Connect on the <Provider> row. The Notion setup dialog no longer
names an "Add connection menu". The preview-env connectors flows
(CON-1 to CON-7) now check the catalog: 12 rows, the views, the search,
and the Connect actions, with no cards or Workspace detail in the
catalog.

  really differs. Below lg the open pane hides the conversation and has
  no Maximize, so the plays check the pane header there. Below md the

  the options that a later refetch of the list uses.

  story does.

cases.brief:
Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources (#529)

* Make the default link teal, not blue

DESIGN.md makes teal the one link accent and allows no second accent.
The primary variant of the shared Link component was blue, so each
link that used the default was blue. It is now teal: teal-400 on the
dark product floor, teal-300 on hover.

Other blue in the UI is not a link and does not change here: the
AlertDialog icon, the ListBox and TagGroup selection, ProgressBar, and
the chat status spinner.


* Add a Switch component

An on/off setting that applies at once, with its label on the right. It
uses the React Aria Switch, the focus ring of the other controls, and
teal for "on". The automatic upgrades setting of Workspace settings is
its first user.


* Workspace settings as one card for each part, with the live work in the sources

Workspace settings showed the state of a Workspace in several places:
status tags in the header, a Status group with a headline, and an
"Ingesting now" list that repeated the sources below it without their
state. A user could not see at once what needed them or what ran.

Each part of the Workspace is now a card: Upgrades, Sources, Knowledge
graph, Repository, Workspace, and Danger zone. Each card states its
state one time, in its body, and holds its own settings and actions.
A line at the top names the parts that need the user and the parts at
work, with a link to each card. A card that needs the user has an
amber edge. A link to #upgrades still lands on the Upgrades card.

Upgrades:
- Each upgrade that needs the user or runs now is a row with a dot.
  Its facts are in one muted line, and its action is a small button on
  the right of the title. Each row keeps its own start and check.
- Automatic upgrades is a switch with one line of help.
- The format shows as "Format 3, the latest", with a tooltip that says
  what a format is.
- History shows the five newest upgrades. "Show all" shows the rest in
  a scroll area. Each row opens to its description, check, spend,
  steps, and reports.
- The card shows no cost estimate, as CTX-894 decided.

Sources:
- Each source shows its live work in its own row: the word of the run
  that is the furthest (for example "Publishing"), and its time. "N
  runs" opens each run with its stage, its count, a bar, and why it
  waits. The separate "Ingesting now" list is gone.
- A source with a problem shows the problem, also while it syncs. The
  live work then shows under the row.
- Each connector is an accordion. It opens by itself when it works,
  needs attention, or waits for a merge. Headers, rows, and runs share
  one column grid, so the dots, the times, and the actions line up.
- The create form and the setup guide keep the table layout.

Knowledge graph: the hydrate state, the error of a failed hydrate, the
indexing of the newest commit, the projection lag, and the skipped
files, in one card.

Repository: write access is one line with its fix. A problem keeps the
title and the facts of the alert that it replaces, and is an alert.

StatusTag and WorkspaceIngestingNow have no users left and are
removed. groupSourceRuns has unit tests. The stories of the pane, the
upgrades, and the surface assert the new layout, and new stories cover
the live work, the source problems, and a long history.


* Wait for the state in the settings and upgrades plays

The play timing check of CI refuses expect(await findBy...).toBeVisible().
These five assertions now wait with waitFor and getBy, as the Storybook
skill says.


* Fix the findings of the three-axis review of Workspace settings

Spec:
- A repository with live work shows in the GitHub list also when it is
  not in the first five rows.
- The Sources card says when it loads the live work.
- The compact repository status has its hint again, as a tip and for a
  screen reader, as the table row does.
- The link of a source that waits for its merge has its external-link
  icon and says that it opens GitHub in a new tab.
- The summary counts a format that ctxpipe checks as work, as the
  Upgrades card does. One state (upgradesState) gives both.
- A read-only Workspace keeps the sentence of today's alert, also when
  no connection reads the repository.

Simplicity:
- upgradesState replaces upgradeHeadline, and the status of an item is
  a label: no reader used the line, the class, or the pulse.
- groupSourceRuns keys the runs on their kind and name, not on a title
  that the lookup made again, and leaves out a re-ingestion as it does
  a hydrate. ingestionItemTitle has no reader left.
- One helper scrolls to a linked connector in both layouts, and only
  the pane scrolls (scrollToPaneTop). The accordion reads the URL hash
  after the first render, so the server and the browser agree.
- One "compact" flag selects the row layout, and the add action of a
  connector is made one time.
- The summary uses the rule of the GitHub rows for a repository that
  needs attention.
- One map holds the title of each card.

Standards:
- A story with plays for the Switch component.
- Named spacing values in place of arbitrary values.
- One-off values are in the functions that use them.
- The format tooltip uses the house Tooltip.
- Comments do not name the "Status group" or the "Ingesting now" list
  any more.

Show one Status group at the top of Workspace settings (CTX-980) (#485)

* Show one Status group at the top of Workspace settings (CTX-980)

The group says first if the user must act: Needs you, Working (no
action needed), or Up to date. Items show in a Needs you list and a
Working now list. A re-ingestion shows its spend so far. History shows
a count and the date of the last applied item. The intro is one line
that is true for both kinds of upgrade, and shows only while an item
is open.


* Look for the Needs you headline in its own row in the stories (CTX-980)

The Needs you list heading has the same word, so a page-wide text query
found two elements.


* Fix the Status group review findings and add the automatic-upgrades toggle

- One clock in the Status group: the headline and the cards change together
  when a checking state ends after a minute.
- A re-ingestion that waits for an open format upgrade goes in the group of
  that upgrade and counts one time. ingestion_v2_off is Working.
- The format health is an input of the headline: a format file that ctxpipe
  cannot read needs you; a format below the newest with no item is Working.
- Automatic upgrades: GET /upgrades/automatic reads the setting from git at
  the tip (no poll); POST takes { mode: manual | automatic }. The Status group
  shows the setting with Turn on and Turn off.
- One tone map for the tags, one pass for the groups, a skeleton with the box
  of the loaded state, "Spend:" for an applied item, UTC history dates,
  "Review upgrade" buttons, and docs for the Status group.


* Fix the toggle pending state, the clock story wait, and the tests that the mode body changed


* Make the automatic-upgrades setting take no body and name each cause

- POST .../upgrades/automatic takes no body or an empty body as `automatic`.
  A body that is not sent as JSON gets a 400 with the fix.
- GET returns `{ mode, reason }`. It reads the head of the default branch, so
  a saved setting shows at once. `reason` is `no_tip`, `invalid_format` or
  `unreadable` (logged, with no secret).
- The 409 of POST names the cause and the fix.
- setUpgradeMode sends only `upgrades`. The job keeps the format of the tree.
- The toggle shows the cause and the fix when ctxpipe cannot read the
  setting. The mode query does not go stale for 5 min and does not read
  again on window focus. Only `automatic` reads the upgrades list again.
- HTTP tests: a plain member reads (200) and cannot change (403) the
  setting; an admin sends no body, an empty body and each mode.
- Card titles are h4. A working card no longer says "No action needed".


* Give an empty setting body to the JSON validator as {}, and wait for the setting line

Hono parses the JSON body from the cached text, so an empty body with a JSON
content type still failed with 400. The middleware now sends a new request
with the body {}. The InvalidFormatFile play reads the line in waitFor.


* Read the upgrade setting with a trees-only fetch and a short cache, and test the 202 path


* Give the 202 test a real owner session


* Reopen the database pool before the seed cleanup


* Give the JSON validator a lowercase content type when the header differs only in case


* Show ingestion work in the Working part of the Status group

The "Ingesting now" list is no longer a separate settings group. It shows
under Working now in the Status group. Ingestion work makes the headline
"Working" when nothing needs the user. Needs you still wins.

The sidebar pulse and the Status headline read the same org ingestion
query through one hook, useWorkspaceIngesting, so they always agree.


* Keep the org ingestion read private to its module

connection row only, with the same rule as the isInstalled field of each
provider status route. Thus the connector catalog can show one state for

short teal mark while data-marked is set. The catalog Fix action finds
the card with this hook, not with a text search.

Add connection is now a two-pane dialog that reads one registry
(features/connectors/catalog/registry.tsx). The left pane has the views
All, Connected, one view for each group, and Coming soon, each with a
count. The right pane has one row for each connector, with the worst
state of its connections and one action: Connect, Add another, or Ask
for it. A row with a connection that needs a reconnect or has an

card of that connection, and marks it for a moment. A search in the

stay as they were. The Add buttons and the old catalog dialog are
removed. Ask for it records a connector_request action through the

product name only. Add a changeset for the release.

installed rows without the site or the token (Confluence, Slack, Linear,
Notion), a hosted GitHub draft without App credentials, and empty Linear
and PagerDuty drafts that the list must not show.

The connectors list copied the isInstalled rule of each status route by
hand on raw JSON. Now models/connection-status.ts has one install rule
for each provider. The list applies the rule to the parsed stored config.
The Confluence, Slack, Notion, and PagerDuty status routes apply the same
rule to the connection that they resolve. Linear keeps
linearConnectionIsInstalled for both. The status values are one const
array: the TypeScript type and the z.enum of the route come from it.

(ariaHideOutside). It keeps only the live announcer and the elements
with data-react-aria-top-layer. The root Toaster is now in such an
element, so that a screen reader announces the "Ask for it" toast of
the connector catalog, and each other toast that shows over a modal.


* Connector catalog: the registry owns each start; Fix marks the card (CTX-1078)

The registry is now the one place that knows how a connector starts.
Each available entry has an async start: it makes any draft, then gives
the setup that the page opens, or nothing when the start runs on its own
(the GitHub App popup). useConnectorStart has no GitHub branch, and the
Connectors page has no opener for each connector: it keeps one setup
state for its mounted setup dialogs. The display order of the cards
comes from the registry order.

The catalog rows switch on the availability with a never check, so a new
availability makes TypeScript show each place to handle. A row shows
its state with ConnectorHealthIndicator, the same chip as the cards; only
the "N connected" label is new.

Fix sets a marked connection in the page state. The card shows a ring
and the hidden text "Needs your attention" on its expand control, and
after the modal closes it scrolls into view and takes the focus. The mark
goes after 2 s. Each card has one connection anchor id
(connectionAnchorId), which Fix and the new GitHub draft scroll use.

Also: remove the onFlowStarted and onDraftCreated options of
useGithubConnectFlow and onInstallFlowStarted of the self-hosted wizard,
which no caller used. Tests and plays take the view counts from the
registry. The GitHub card story gets its args, so its 4 allowed type
errors go.


* Confluence card: show the product name only (CTX-1078)

The card said "Atlassian Confluence" and the catalog says "Confluence".
The card now says "Confluence" too. The plays read the new name.


* Docs: start each connector from its catalog row (CTX-1078)

Each page that said "Add connection, then <Provider>" or "Connectors ->
Add connection -> <Provider>" now says: select Add connection, then
select Connect on the <Provider> row. The Notion setup dialog no longer
names an "Add connection menu". The preview-env connectors flows
(CON-1 to CON-7) now check the catalog: 12 rows, the views, the search,
and the Connect actions, with no cards or Workspace detail in the
catalog.

element, so that a screen reader announces the "Ask for it" toast of
the connector catalog, and each other toast that shows over a modal.

The registry is now the one place that knows how a connector starts.
Each available entry has an async start: it makes any draft, then gives
the setup that the page opens, or nothing when the start runs on its own
(the GitHub App popup). useConnectorStart has no GitHub branch, and the
Connectors page has no opener for each connector: it keeps one setup
state for its mounted setup dialogs. The display order of the cards
comes from the registry order.

availability makes TypeScript show each place to handle. A row shows
its state with ConnectorHealthIndicator, the same chip as the cards; only

and the hidden text "Needs your attention" on its expand control, and
after the modal closes it scrolls into view and takes the focus. The mark

(connectionAnchorId), which Fix and the new GitHub draft scroll use.

which no caller used. Tests and plays take the view counts from the
registry. The GitHub card story gets its args, so its 4 allowed type
errors go.

The card said "Atlassian Confluence" and the catalog says "Confluence".
The card now says "Confluence" too. The plays read the new name.


* Docs: start each connector from its catalog row (CTX-1078)

Each page that said "Add connection, then <Provider>" or "Connectors ->
Add connection -> <Provider>" now says: select Add connection, then
select Connect on the <Provider> row. The Notion setup dialog no longer
names an "Add connection menu". The preview-env connectors flows

cases.brief:
Show when a Workspace ingests: a sidebar pulse and an Ingesting now list (CTX-959) (#465)

* Read the active ingestion work of a Workspace from its workflow runs (CTX-959)

Add GET /workspaces/{slug}/ingestion for Workspace settings and
GET /workspace-ingestion for the sidebar. Each item has its kind, name,
stage, progress and start time. A run that waits for an earlier run of
the same repository has the stage waiting. A hydrate of the newest commit
shows only after 30 s.


* Format the ingestion read test


* Show when a Workspace ingests: a sidebar pulse and an Ingesting now list (CTX-959)

The SideNav row of a Workspace with active ingestion shows a teal pulse
with the text "Ingesting N sources". The pulse stops with reduced
motion. Workspace settings has an Ingesting now group with the stage,
the count and the time so far of each run, in the upgrade progress
pattern.


* Stop the status pulse with reduced motion and fix the collapsed row story


* Add a changeset for the ingesting indicator (CTX-959)


* Keep the route index change to the two new lines


* Fix the type errors and unused exports of the ingesting indicator

Use SideNavTooltip for the dot, give the demo state its type, make the
test request callbacks async, and keep internal names unexported.


* Bound the active ingestion read and keep the sidebar read light

Each branch of the run query is now a range scan of the index
(namespace_id, workflow_name, status, created_at) with a constant start
time: one day for ingestion and sync runs, three hours for hydrates. The
query selects only the input keys the read uses. It excludes shadow runs,
non-connection syncs, and fast or older hydrates before the limit of 200.

A root list that does not unzip, or that is larger than 32 MiB unzipped,
hides only the progress of its run. The sidebar read returns counts per
Workspace and does not read the steps. Both polls use 5 s while work runs.


* Do not export the sidebar count type


* Drop unused IngestionRoot import after merge


* Show the code index and resolved destinations in the ingestion view

- Read `repository-ingestion` runs, so the code index of a repository
  shows as the `indexing` stage. This also applies to a Workspace below
  format 3.
- After the `resolve` step of an ingestion v2 run, take its destinations
  from the step output. Before that step, match the source files.
- In the sidebar count, do not count an upgrade re-ingestion next to its
  own ingestion v2 run.
- Give only repository runs a stage, and give a hydrate no name.
- Stop the poll when a read fails (pollWhileOk).
- Use the provider label from SOURCE_SCOPES and repositoryNameFromGitUrl.
- Run the reduced-motion story in the required set, and make the plays
  wait for a settled state.
- Give the test fixtures ages that stay on one side of each threshold.


* Start the ingesting demo story with work so the sidebar dot shows

The sidebar reads an idle org once a minute, so the demo never showed the dot.

cases.brief:
Add workspaces launch GIF to README; show the unverified email toast as a notice (#478)

* Add Workspaces launch GIF to README


* Show the unverified email sign-in toast as a notice, not an error

better-auth-ui sends each sign-in failure as an error toast. When the
email is not verified, Better Auth sends a new link (sendOnSignIn), so
the message is a notice. The AuthUIProvider toast callback now shows
that message as an info toast. Other toasts keep their variant.

The "Sign-in, unverified email" story proves it: MSW answers sign-in
with 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, and the play expects an info toast.

* Add a changeset for the unverified email sign-in toast

cases.brief:
Buildkite connector on Workspace sources (CTX-717) (#522)

* Add the Buildkite connector (port of PR 419)

Port the Buildkite connector onto current main. The change set comes
from PR 419 (feat/buildkite-connector).

- Mirror the latest finished builds of selected pipelines into a
  Workspace source.
- Add the connection, webhook, sync, and UI setup.
- Rename the ADR to ADR-057.
- Put the docs in the new guide page structure.


* Keep the ADR-057 row in the index table, and split a long docs sentence

* Add the changeset for the Buildkite connector


* Read the Buildkite event name from the signed body

The signature does not cover the X-Buildkite-Event header. A replayed
signed ping could queue a sync. The route now reads the event from the
signed JSON body.


* Clean up the Buildkite connector code

Use ctxpipe in product text. Log with getLogger. Use the shared Link
component. Remove the no-op kept filter. Require the status field.
Rename the OpenAPI error helper. Add one pipelines path helper.
Make the changeset bump @ctxpipe/aws-cdk.


* Fix the Buildkite docs

Name both Buildkite hosts. Describe the blocked build files as the code
does. Split long steps. Use the sibling heading style. Fix the guide
index so that it does not contradict itself.


* Fix ADR-057 and the ADR index

State the pipeline caps, the signed event name, and the GraphQL host.
Add buildkite to the ADR-050 provider list. Reserve ADR-058 and ADR-059.


* Allow a connector with no config file in the source-connectors skill


* Update the Buildkite setup story for the shared Link


* Name the GraphQL host only for the connect check, and write organization owner or admin

* Use the teal external link in the Buildkite setup

Match the other connector setup dialogs: a teal link with an external-link icon.


* Add a way to create a Workspace from the Workspace step

When the organization has no Workspace, the step now tells the user what to do
and shows a Create a Workspace button.


* Cover the no-Workspace step and the self-host troubleshooting in the Buildkite docs

* Wait for the empty-state text in the NoWorkspaces story

The play read a state of a findBy result outside waitFor, which the play
timing check refuses. Use waitFor with getBy, as the check asks.


* Accept ADR-057 (CTX-717)

The connectors area owner accepted the Buildkite connector decision in
the review of the pull request.
